name: Eastside Commons Fridge
hours: 24/7 — take what you need, leave what you can
description: Community fridge stocked daily by neighbors, local restaurants, and the urban farm collective. Fresh produce Tuesdays and Fridays.

name: Marisol's Kitchen Pantry
description: Volunteer-run pantry operating out of the back of a tienda. Dry goods, canned food, and hot breakfast on Sunday mornings. No ID required.

name: Tenants Together East Bay
address: Above Blue Star Bakery, 2201 23rd Ave, Oakland, CA
description: Know-your-rights workshops, eviction defense clinics, and free one-on-one consultations with housing advocates. They will help you respond to an unlawful eviction notice — come early.

name: East Oakland Housing Clinic
address: Community Room, 7000 Foothill Blvd, Oakland, CA
description: Free legal clinic covering habitability issues, security deposits, and lease violations. Bring your lease and any written notices. Interpreters available in Spanish and Mam.

name: Defremery Park Seating Grove
description: A quiet grove with benches, chess tables, and a community bulletin board. Older residents gather here most mornings. The board has housed ride-share notices, Spanish tutoring offers, and more.

name: Cesar Chavez Library Reading Room
description: Free wifi, air conditioning, printing, notary services, and librarians who will help you navigate every bureaucracy you are afraid of. Meeting rooms available at no cost with 48-hour notice.

name: Victor's Radio & Electronics Repair
description: Victor has been fixing radios, lamps, and small appliances for 30 years. He accepts no payment but will take produce or conversation. Call ahead — he is often in the garden.
contact: Ask at the blue house on the corner

name: Bike Kitchen East
description: Community bike shop with free tools and used parts. Volunteers teach basic maintenance, and you can earn a bike by working a few shifts. Youth programs Friday afternoons.

name: Rosa's Textile Studio
hours: By appointment and open studio Sundays 1–5pm
description: Rosa weaves and sells handmade textiles rooted in Zapotec tradition. She also repairs clothing and teaches small sewing workshops. First-generation Oakland maker.

name: Fruitvale Urban Growers
description: A collective of six backyard farmers selling seasonal produce at below-market prices. Accepts EBT. Ask about their seed library and composting drop-off.

name: St. Benedict Church Basement
description: The church basement is open to community groups every Thursday with no religious requirement or affiliation. Tables, chairs, a projector, and a functioning kitchen. 40-person capacity.

name: Sal's Barbershop Corner
description: Sal has run this corner shop for 22 years. It is genuinely one of the last places in this neighborhood where strangers still talk to each other without a device in their hand. News travels here.

name: Eastside Mutual Aid Network
address: Mobile — find them via signal group
description: Neighbors helping neighbors with transportation to medical appointments, childcare swaps, emergency groceries, and utility bill support. Run entirely by local residents. No bureaucracy. Text to be connected.

name: Laundry Day Collective
description: Free laundry day at a local laundromat. Detergent provided. Volunteers bring food and conversation. Started by two neighbors during a hard winter and never stopped.

name: Eastside Worker Co-op Incubator
description: A small office of people who have converted three local businesses to worker ownership. Free consulting, workshops, and mentorship for anyone thinking about starting or converting a cooperative.

name: Coliseum Corridor Buying Club
hours: Monthly meetings — check the community board
description: Bulk purchasing group for staple goods: rice, oil, beans, cleaning supplies. Dramatically reduces grocery costs. Currently 40 households and growing. Looking for a space to expand.

name: Libros Libres (Free Books)
description: A neighbor's free library box that expanded to three shelves on the porch. Spanish-language section, children's books, zines, and a small collection on tenant rights and local history.

name: Oakland Tool Library
description: Borrow tools instead of buying them. Drills, saws, ladders, gardening equipment, and specialty tools for home repair. Annual membership is $50, or volunteer two hours a month.

name: Amara Abebe, Herbalist & Healer
description: Traditional Ethiopian herbalism, prenatal support, and community health education. Sliding scale fees. Amara has been offering care in this neighborhood for 15 years and is a trusted anchor of the health commons.
contact: referred through the mutual aid network

name: Bancroft Commons Community Garden
description: 24 plot community garden with a tool shed, rain barrels, and a communal composting station. Waitlist for plots is 6 months, but volunteers can work the common areas immediately — and take home produce.

name: Pinole Street Supper Club
address: Rotating homes — subscribe to get the address
description: Potluck supper club that has been running for four years without a name until someone insisted. A genuine cross-section of the neighborhood at one long table. You bring what you can.

name: Foothill Tool & Skill Share
address: 3900 Foothill Blvd (back parking lot), Oakland, CA
hours: Every last Saturday of the month, 9am–1pm
description: Monthly swap where neighbors trade tools, skills, and services. Plumber trades a house call for a haircut. Electrician teaches a workshop. Seed swap table always present. Organized entirely by residents.

name: Naomi's Secondhand & Alterations
description: Decades-old secondhand shop with in-house alterations, mending, and a pay-what-you-can rack for families who need it. Naomi knows every regular by name and has refused to relocate despite three rent increases.

name: East Bay Permanent Real Estate Cooperative
description: A community land trust and real estate co-op working to permanently remove land from the speculative market. Active member campaigns in this neighborhood. Monthly orientation for new community members.

name: Nourish East Oakland
description: Hot meals, no questions asked. Run by a coalition of local faith communities. The line is long on Mondays but moves fast. They are always looking for volunteers and food donations from restaurants.
